text:
# Accessibility Services

- The library building is wheelchair accessible, with an accessible
  entrance at the front of the building and an elevator to the second
  floor.
- Large-print books and audiobooks are available throughout the
  collection; ask the front desk for the large-print catalogue section.
- A dedicated accessible workstation with screen-reading software is
  available in the Computer Lab; booking is recommended but not required.
- Patrons who are unable to visit in person due to a disability may
  request home delivery of up to 5 items at a time through the
  Homebound Services program; contact the front desk to enroll.
title: Accessibility Services

text:
# Borrowing and Renewal Policy

## Borrowing
- Standard members may borrow up to 5 items at a time.
- Premium members may borrow up to 15 items at a time.
- Most items have a loan period of 2 weeks (Standard) or 3 weeks (Premium).
- Some popular new-release titles are short-loan items: 1 week (Standard) or
  2 weeks (Premium). The loan period is always shown on the item's catalogue
  record.
title: Borrowing and Renewal Policy

text:
Some popular new-release titles are short-loan items: 1 week (Standard) or 2 weeks (Premium). The loan period is always shown on the item's catalogue record.

## Renewals
- Items may be renewed up to 2 times, as long as no other patron has placed
  a hold on the item.
- Renewals can be done online, by phone, or at the front desk, up to 2 days
  before the due date.
- An item with a hold from another patron cannot be renewed and must be
  returned by its due date.
title: Borrowing and Renewal Policy

## Returns
- Items can be returned at the front desk or through the outside book drop,
  which is checked each morning when the library opens.
- Items returned in the book drop after closing are credited to the

title: Borrowing and Renewal Policy

text:
# Children's and Youth Programs

- The library runs a weekly Storytime session for ages 2-5, every
  Saturday at 11:00 AM in the Children's Corner.
- A Summer Reading Challenge runs from June through August for school-age
  children, with small prizes for reading milestones.
- After-school homework help is available Monday to Thursday, 3:30 PM -
  5:30 PM, staffed by volunteer tutors; no registration required.
- Children's library cards (for patrons under 13) have the same borrowing
  limits as a Standard membership but no overdue fines - a reminder notice
  is sent instead.
title: Children's and Youth Programs

text:
# Library Code of Conduct

- The library is a shared, quiet space; patrons are asked to keep phone
  calls and conversations to designated areas where possible.
- Food is not permitted near computers or in the stacks; covered
  beverages are allowed throughout the building.
- Children under 8 must be accompanied by a caregiver at all times, except
  during supervised programs such as Storytime.
- Disruptive behavior, including harassment of staff or other patrons,
  may result in a verbal warning, a temporary suspension of library
  privileges, or removal from the premises for repeated violations.
title: Library Code of Conduct

text:
# Digital Resources and E-Books

- Riverbend Community Library offers e-books and audiobooks through its
  digital lending app, available to all members with a valid library card.
- Digital loans follow a 2-week loan period and are returned
  automatically - there are no late fees on digital items.
- Standard members may borrow up to 3 digital items at a time; Premium
  members may borrow up to 10.
- The library also provides free access to several online research
  databases and a language-learning platform, accessible with a library
  card login from home or on-site.
title: Digital Resources and E-Books

text:
# Donations and Volunteering

## Book donations
- The library accepts gently used book donations during open hours at
  the front desk.
- Donated items are added to the collection, the Friends of the Library
  used-book sale, or a community giveaway shelf, depending on condition
  and current collection needs.
- The library cannot issue tax-donation receipts for individual item
  values but can provide a general donation acknowledgment letter on
  request.
title: Donations and Volunteering

## Volunteering
- Volunteer opportunities include shelving, the Summer Reading Challenge,
  after-school tutoring, and the Friends of the Library book sale.
- Volunteers must be at least 14 years old (or 12 with a parent
  volunteering alongside them) and complete a short orientation session.
title: Donations and Volunteering

text:
# Library Events and Workshops

- The library hosts a monthly Book Club on the first Tuesday of each
  month at 6:30 PM, open to all members; the current title is posted at
  the front desk and on the library's events board.
- Periodic workshops (resume writing, basic computer skills, tax-season
  help) are announced at least 2 weeks in advance via the library's
  events board and mailing list.
- Event registration, where required, is free and can be done online or
  at the front desk; walk-ins are accommodated as space allows.
title: Library Events and Workshops

text:
# Fax and Notary Services

- Fax service is available at the front desk for $1.00 per page (sending)
  and $0.25 per page (receiving).
- A notary public is available on-site Tuesday and Thursday afternoons,
  1:00 PM - 4:00 PM, free of charge for library members; photo ID is
  required for notarization.
title: Fax and Notary Services

text:
# Holds and Reservations

- Patrons may place a hold on any item that is currently checked out. - Standard members may have 1 active hold at a time; Premium members may   have up to 2 active holds at a time. - Holds are filled in the order they were placed (first come, first served). - When a held item becomes available, the patron is notified by email or   phone and has a pickup window to collect it: 3 days for Standard members,   5 days for Premium members. - If the pickup window passes without collection, the hold is cancelled and   the item moves to the next patron in the queue.

- An item with an active hold cannot be renewed by the patron currently   holding it..
title: Holds and Reservations

text:
# Interlibrary Loan

- If an item is not in the Riverbend Community Library catalogue, patrons   may request it through interlibrary loan from partner library systems   in the region. - Requests can be submitted online or at the front desk; typical turnaround   is 5-10 business days depending on the lending library. - Interlibrary loan items follow a shorter loan period (2 weeks, no   renewals) due to lending-library restrictions, and are not eligible for   the standard overdue fine schedule - a flat $1.00/day fine applies to   overdue interlibrary loan items, as these affect another library's   patrons directly.
title: Interlibrary Loan

text: - There is no fee to request an interlibrary loan, but a lost or damaged   interlibrary loan item is charged at the lending library's stated   replacement value..
title: Interlibrary Loan

text:
# Getting a Library Card

- Library cards are free for all residents and students in the service   area. - To apply in person, bring a valid photo ID and proof of current address   (a utility bill, lease agreement, or official mail dated within the   last 60 days). - Cards for patrons under 18 require a parent or guardian's signature on   the application. - A digital library card is also available through the library's mobile   app once a physical card has been issued; the digital card can be used   for checkout at the self-service kiosks.
title: Getting a Library Card

text: - Lost cards can be replaced at the front desk for a $2.00 fee; report a   lost card promptly to avoid unauthorized use..
title: Getting a Library Card

text:
# Library Hours

- Monday to Friday: 9:00 AM - 8:00 PM
- Saturday: 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM
- Sunday: Closed

## Holiday hours
The library follows a modified holiday schedule around major public
holidays; closures are posted at the front entrance and on the library's
notice board at least one week in advance. The library is closed on New
Year's Day, Independence Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day.

## Book drop
The outside book drop is accessible 24 hours a day, including when the
library is closed.
title: Library Hours

text:
# Lost and Found

- Personal items (not library materials) left in the building are held at
  the front desk for 30 days before being donated or discarded.
- Valuable items (wallets, phones, jewelry) are logged and held for 90
  days.
- For lost or damaged library materials, see the Overdue Fines and Lost
  Items policy.
title: Lost and Found

text:
# Meeting Room Booking

- The library has 1 large meeting room (capacity 30) available for
  community groups, book clubs, and educational workshops.
- Meeting room booking is free for Premium members and community
  organizations; Standard members may book it for a $10/session fee.
- Bookings must be made at least 3 days in advance through the front
  desk.
- The room includes a projector, whiteboard, and seating for up to 30
  people; audio/visual equipment should be requested at time of booking.
title: Meeting Room Booking

text:
# Membership Freeze and Cancellation

- Premium members who will be away for an extended period (60+ days) may
  request a membership freeze; the remaining paid months are added back
  once the membership is reactivated.
- A freeze does not cancel existing loans or holds, which remain subject
  to normal due dates and fines.
- Memberships can be cancelled at any time at the front desk; any
  outstanding fines or unreturned items must be settled before
  cancellation is finalized.
- Premium membership fees are non-refundable once the annual period has
  started, except in cases of relocation outside the service area, which
  may be prorated on request.
title: Membership Freeze and Cancellation

text:
# Membership Tiers

Riverbend Community Library offers two membership tiers.

## Standard Membership (free)
- Borrow up to 5 items at a time
- 14-day loan period (2 weeks)
- 1 active hold at a time
- No annual fee

## Premium Membership ($25/year)
- Borrow up to 15 items at a time
- 21-day loan period (3 weeks)
- Up to 2 active holds at a time
- Extended pickup window (5 days instead of 3) when a held item becomes available
- Free access to the library's meeting rooms (see Meeting Room Booking policy)

text:
# Overdue Fines and Lost Items

## Overdue fines
- $0.25 per day, per item.
- The maximum fine for any single item is capped at $10.00.
- Fines accrue daily until the item is returned or the cap is reached.
- A patron's account is blocked from new borrowing once their total
  outstanding fines exceed $15.00, until the balance is paid down or
  items are returned.
title: Overdue Fines and Lost Items

text:
A patron's account is blocked from new borrowing once their total outstanding fines exceed $15.00, until the balance is paid down or items are returned.

## Lost or damaged items
- If an item is not returned within 30 days of its due date, it is marked
  lost and the patron is charged the replacement cost of the item plus a
  $5.00 processing fee.
- If a lost item is later found and returned in good condition within 60
  days of being marked lost, the replacement cost is refunded; the $5.00
  processing fee is non-refundable.
- Damaged items (water damage, torn pages, missing components such as a
  DVD case insert) are assessed individually by library staff, who may
  charge a partial or full replacement fee depending on the extent of
  the damage.
title: Overdue Fines and Lost Items

text:
# Printing, Scanning, and Computer Use

- The library has 10 public computers available on a first-come,
  first-served basis, with a 1-hour session limit when others are waiting.
- Black-and-white printing is $0.10/page; color printing is $0.50/page.
- Scanning to a USB drive or email is free.
- Free Wi-Fi is available throughout the building for patrons with their
  own devices; no login is required.
title: Printing, Scanning, and Computer Use

text:
# Study Room Booking

- The library has 4 private study rooms, each seating up to 6 people.
- Rooms can be booked online or at the front desk up to 7 days in advance.
- Maximum booking length is 2 hours per session; a room may be re-booked
  for an additional 2 hours if no one else has reserved it immediately
  after.
- Bookings are free for both Standard and Premium members.
- A no-show (not checking in within 15 minutes of the booking start time)
  releases the room for walk-in use.
title: Study Room Booking
